newsitem.title: USA: Texas "yard of horrors" yields mysterious bones.
newsitem.headline: Texas "yard of horrors" yields mysterious bones.

text.p: The search for a missing woman has turned up hundreds of human bone fragments buried in her backyard, but no evidence of her, police said Tuesday.

DNA tests indicate the bones found so far in what news reports describe as "the little backyard of horrors" belong to as many as three people, but none of them is Monika Rizzo, a 44-year-old government employee not seen since late May.
"We're at a loss about who those remains belong to," said San Antonio deputy police chief Albert Ortiz.
Police were searching for more remains while pondering the mystery of how the bones got there. They suspect foul play, but said they have not yet got enough evidence to conclude there was a murder.
An anonymous caller advised police they would find Rizzo's body buried in the backyard of the house she shared with husband Leonard Rizzo, which led them to start digging on Friday.

Instead, they found the bone fragments scattered through the yard covered by a thin layer of dirt. There was also a well-used backyard barbecue pit that police say may have been used to burn body parts.
The bones were chopped up into small pieces, as if they had been run through a grinder, police said.
Police have questioned the woman's husband about the findings, but no legal action has been taken. His lawyer, Bruce Smith, told reporters Leonard Rizzo had done nothing wrong.

Monika Rizzo has not been seen since she left her office for lunch on May 27. Her disappearance was not reported until her parents notified police on June 10 after hearing she was gone from one of the Rizzos' two sons.
San Antonio Police Department spokesman Al Ballew said a team of archaeologists from the University of Texas at San Antonio had been called in to help sift through the site.
The dig would go on until police were content they had found all the remains, he said.
"They have found a lot of bone fragments already and they're finding more every day," Ballew said.
